cards.explanation: The question Jesus asks is whether those Galileans were worse sinners than the other Galileans. He says, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?" I think this one hurts, friends, because real people died here. He doesn't answer it with a shrug, either. He's about to say something that matters for everyone standing there.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "No, I tell you." Then He adds, "But unless you repent, you too will all perish." He doesn't agree that those Galileans were worse than the rest, friends. He points the crowd to something else.

The word Jesus uses is repent. He says, "But unless you repent, you too will all perish." And He says it twice, once about the Galileans and once about the eighteen under the tower (Luke 13:3, 5). When Jesus repeats something, I stop stirring and listen, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus asks whether they were "…more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?" and He answers, "No, I tell you." I think this one is heavy, friends, because eighteen people died when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them. Then He gives the same warning He just gave.
The man finds no fruit at all. He "…went to look for fruit on it but did not find any." Not a little, friends, and not some. The tree is planted in his vineyard, and that's where he looks.

The owner tells the keeper to cut it down. He says, "Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?" It's a strong word to the keeper of the vineyard, friends, and he doesn't soften it. Three years of searching and no fruit is how he gets there.

The word is year. The keeper says, "…leave it alone again this year…" He doesn't argue that the tree deserves forever, friends. He asks for one more round. And he speaks up for the tree right after the owner says to cut it down.

The keeper's plan is to dig around the tree and fertilize it. He says, "…until I dig around it and fertilize it." He isn't just asking the owner to wait, friends. He says he'll do the work himself during that year.

The answer is False. The keeper makes no promise. He says, "If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down." Notice he says "if," friends. He doesn't say what will happen, and the parable doesn't tell us either.
